title: Verb (+ object) + to … (I want you to …)

exercises.instruction: Complete the questions. Use do you want me to … ? or would you like me to … ? with these verbs (and any other necessary words):

parts: Do you have enough money, or do you want
answers: or do you want me to lend you some

parts: Shall I leave the window open, or would you
answers: or would you like me to shut it

parts: Do you know how to use the printer, or would
answers: or would you like me to show you

parts: Did you hear what I said, or do
answers: or do you want me to repeat it

parts: Can I go now, or do
answers: or do you want me to wait

exercises.instruction: Read the situations and complete the sentences.
exercises.scene:
💬 What was said, and how it was answered (read the descriptions):
2. Why don't you come and stay with us? — That would be nice.
3. Don't forget to call Joe. — No, I won't forget.
4. Be careful on the stairs. — Don't worry. I will.
5. Can you give me a hand with this? — Sure.

answers: her to give him a hand

exercises.instruction: Read the first sentence of each pair, then complete the second one so that it means the same.

items.cue: 1st: I was surprised that it rained.
1st: Don’t stop him doing what he wants.
1st: Tom looks older when he wears glasses.
1st: I think you should know the truth.
1st: At first I didn’t want to apply for the job, but Sarah persuaded me.
answers: me to apply for the job

items.cue: 1st: My lawyer said I shouldn’t say anything to the police.
answers: me not to say anything to the police

items.cue: 1st: I was told that I shouldn’t believe everything he says.
answers: not to believe everything he says

items.cue: 1st: If you’ve got a car, you are able to get around more easily.
answers: you to get around more easily
